properties.name: Western Ghats Montane Forest Corridor
properties.region: Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu
properties.baseline_text: 43,850 sq km canopy cover
properties.comparison_text: 45,120 sq km canopy cover
properties.delta_text: +1,270 sq km (+2.9%) net gain in open/mod forest
properties.primary_driver: Commercial plantation expansion vs core evergreen interior fragmentation
properties.ecological_impact: While total tree canopy expanded due to rubber, coffee and teak plantations, dense evergreen rainforest interior cores suffered linear fragmentation from roads and power lines, impacting endemic arboreal primates (Lion-tailed Macaque).
properties.citation: Forest Survey of India (FSI) — State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2001 & 2021

properties.name: Northeast India Shifting Cultivation Belt
properties.region: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram, Manipur, Meghalaya
properties.baseline_text: 169,825 sq km primary forest
properties.comparison_text: 166,540 sq km remaining forest
properties.delta_text: -3,285 sq km (-1.93%) primary canopy loss
properties.primary_driver: Shortened jhum slash-and-burn cycles, infrastructure, and bamboo flowering degradation
properties.ecological_impact: Traditional 15-20 year rotational jhum cycles shrank to 3-5 years due to demographic pressure, preventing natural canopy regeneration and causing heavy topsoil loss across hilly watershed catchments.
properties.citation: FSI ISFR Assessments 2001–2021; MoEFCC Technical Forest Statistics

properties.name: Sundarbans Deltaic Mangrove Biosphere
properties.baseline_text: 2,081 sq km mangrove cover
properties.comparison_text: 2,114 sq km mangrove cover
properties.delta_text: +33 sq km (+1.58%) net mangrove colonization
properties.primary_driver: Sea-level rise, increased salinity, and frequent super cyclones (Amphan, Yaas)
properties.ecological_impact: While mudbank accretion allowed pioneer mangrove colonization, reduced freshwater flows from the upstream Ganga altered water chemistry, causing freshwater-loving Sundari (Heritiera fomes) trees to decline in favor of saline-tolerant Avicennia marina.
properties.citation: FSI ISFR 2021 Mangrove Cover Assessment; Sundarban Biosphere Reserve Directorate

properties.name: Eastern Ghats Deciduous & Social Forestry Belt
properties.baseline_text: 44,200 sq km forest cover
properties.comparison_text: 47,480 sq km forest cover
properties.delta_text: +3,280 sq km (+7.42%) expansion via community forestry
properties.primary_driver: Vana Samrakshana Samithi (VSS) joint management, agro-forestry, and compensatory afforestation
properties.ecological_impact: Significant green cover gains in open and scrub forest categories, improving ground moisture retention across degraded quartzitic hill slopes, though mono-species eucalyptus and bamboo plantations lack original biodiversity.
properties.citation: FSI Biennial Assessments 2001 vs 2021; Andhra Pradesh Forest Department

properties.name: Central Indian Sal & Teak Wildlife Corridor
properties.baseline_text: 76,400 sq km dense forest
properties.comparison_text: 77,493 sq km dense forest
properties.delta_text: +1,093 sq km (+1.43%) stable tiger corridor core
properties.primary_driver: Project Tiger protected area zoning, Kanha-Pench corridor conservation
properties.ecological_impact: Robust protection of core deciduous forests preserves India's largest metapopulation of Bengal Tigers (Panthera tigris), maintaining vital carbon sinks and perennial headwater catchments of the Narmada and Mahanadi rivers.
properties.citation: FSI ISFR 2021; National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)

properties.name: Gangotri Glacier & Gaumukh Snout
properties.baseline_text: Gaumukh Snout position at 3,920 m (1965 Corona satellite baseline)
properties.comparison_text: Gaumukh Snout shifted to 4,015 m (1,530 m upvalley retreat)
properties.delta_text: -1,530 m retreat (~22 m/year average retreat rate)
properties.primary_driver: Rising surface temperatures, decreasing winter snowfall, and heavy debris-cover detachment
properties.ecological_impact: Accelerated melting thins the main 30.2 km ice trunk, creating moraine collapse at the snout and forming expanding supra-glacial meltwater lakes that threaten flash flood discharge down the Bhagirathi Ganga valley.
properties.citation: Space Applications Centre (SAC - ISRO) Himalayan Glaciers Atlas; Geological Survey of India (GSI) Glaciology Div

properties.name: Siachen Glacier Terminus
properties.baseline_text: 76.5 km ice tongue length; continuous tributary feeds
properties.comparison_text: 71.2 km active tongue; lower 5 km stagnant debris
properties.delta_text: -5.3 km snout detachment & 17% ice volume loss
properties.primary_driver: Global warming, reduced winter accumulation, and military anthropogenic footprint
properties.ecological_impact: World's second longest non-polar glacier is experiencing tributary detachment (e.g. Teram Shehr, Lolofond), thinning ice thickness by up to 100 meters and altering downstream summer melt discharge into the Nubra and Shyok rivers.
properties.citation: ISRO SAC Karakoram Cryosphere Studies; Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG)

properties.name: Chorabari Glacier & Gandhi Sarovar (Kedarnath)
properties.baseline_text: Intact snout feeding stable moraine-dammed lake
properties.comparison_text: 320 m snout retreat with breached moraine lake wall
properties.delta_text: -320 m retreat & catastrophic 2013 GLOF breach
properties.primary_driver: Glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) dynamics, heavy monsoonal cloudbursts
properties.ecological_impact: Site of the tragic June 2013 Kedarnath disaster: unprecedented heavy rain combined with rapid glacial melt burst the Chorabari moraine-dammed lake (Gandhi Sarovar), triggering a catastrophic debris flow that decimated Kedarnath town.
properties.citation: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG) Report on Kedarnath Disaster; SAC-ISRO

properties.name: Zemu Glacier (Kangchenjunga Basin)
properties.baseline_text: 28.0 km length from Kangchenjunga east flank
properties.comparison_text: 25.8 km length with expanding proglacial lake
properties.delta_text: -2.2 km retreat & rapid proglacial lake formation
properties.primary_driver: Rising eastern Himalayan temperatures, accelerated summer ablation
properties.ecological_impact: Zemu is the prime feeder of the Teesta River. Rapid shrinkage is causing heavy supra-glacial pond coalescence, elevating GLOF hazard risk for downstream hydroelectric dams across Sikkim (e.g. Teesta-III Chungthang dam failure precursor).
properties.citation: Geological Survey of India (GSI) Eastern Region Glaciology; Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority

properties.name: Kolhai Glacier ('Goddess of Light')
properties.baseline_text: 13.87 sq km continuous ice expanse
properties.comparison_text: 10.95 sq km heavily fragmented ice mass
properties.delta_text: -21.05% surface area shrinkage
properties.primary_driver: Winter snowfall deficit, black carbon deposition, warming valley temperatures
properties.ecological_impact: Primary water tower for the Kashmir Valley. Rapid shrinkage threatens drinking water supply for Srinagar and irrigation for apple orchards and paddy fields across Anantnag, Pulwama, and Srinagar districts.
properties.citation: University of Kashmir Dept of Earth Sciences Cryosphere Group; SAC-ISRO Glacier Inventory

properties.name: Bara Shigri Glacier (Lahaul-Spiti)
properties.baseline_text: 27.5 km length; largest glacier in Himachal
properties.comparison_text: 26.4 km length; detached tributary glaciers
properties.delta_text: -1,100 m retreat (~19.3 m/year average rate)
properties.primary_driver: Negative mass balance, higher equilibrium line altitude (ELA)
properties.ecological_impact: Historical breach in 1836 dammed the Chandra river creating a massive lake that devastated the valley when it burst. Ongoing retreat is forming new proglacial moraine lakes requiring continuous satellite monitoring.
properties.citation: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG) Chenab Basin Glacier Monograph; GSI

properties.name: Delhi National Capital Region (NCR) Megalopolis
properties.baseline_text: 485 sq km contiguous built-up area
properties.comparison_text: 1,840 sq km contiguous built-up area
properties.delta_text: +1,355 sq km (+279.4%) explosive radial sprawl
properties.primary_driver: Post-economic liberalization rapid urbanization, expressway corridors, real estate conversion
properties.ecological_impact: Impervious concrete sprawl over Aravalli green ridges and Yamuna active floodplains drastically reduced groundwater recharge, causing acute urban flooding during monsoons and intense winter PM2.5 smog trapping.
properties.citation: NRSC Decadal Land Use / Land Cover (LULC) Atlas; Census of India Urban Growth

properties.name: Greater Bengaluru Metropolitan Area (BBMP)
properties.baseline_text: 165 sq km built-up (34% tree canopy, 280 interconnected lakes)
properties.comparison_text: 741 sq km built-up (>78% paved surfaces, <80 living lakes)
properties.delta_text: +576 sq km (+349.1%) massive tech corridor sprawl
properties.primary_driver: IT industry boom, Outer Ring Road and Electronic City construction, lakebed reclamation
properties.ecological_impact: Transformation of the 'Garden City' into a concrete heat island. Loss of >70% of ancient cascading lake networks severed natural storm drainage, triggering severe urban flooding (Bellandur, Varthur) and profound groundwater crisis.
properties.citation: Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Energy & Wetlands Research Group; NRSC LULC

properties.name: Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) Northward Axis
properties.region: Maharashtra (Mumbai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Mira-Bhayandar, Panvel)
properties.baseline_text: 340 sq km built-up area
properties.comparison_text: 910 sq km built-up area
properties.delta_text: +570 sq km (+167.6%) expansion into salt pans & hills
properties.primary_driver: Island city spatial saturation pushing development north and east along rail/freeway spines
properties.ecological_impact: Severe destruction of coastal mangroves and mudflats along Thane Creek and Ulhas estuary; reclamation of Mithi River catchment exacerbated catastrophic urban deluge events (such as the 26 July 2005 flood).
properties.citation: Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA); NRSC Urban Studies

properties.name: Greater Hyderabad & Outer Ring Road (ORR) Grid
properties.baseline_text: 210 sq km built-up footprint
properties.comparison_text: 685 sq km built-up footprint
properties.delta_text: +475 sq km (+226.2%) radial expansion across ORR
properties.primary_driver: Cyberabad IT hub development, 158 km Outer Ring Road expressway, pharma city expansion
properties.ecological_impact: Obliteration of ancient Kakatiya irrigation water tanks (cheruvus) and granitic rock formations; Musi River transformed into an effluent conduit with heavy urban flash-flood vulnerability in low-lying colonies.
properties.citation: Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA); NRSC Decadal LULC

properties.name: Chennai Metropolitan Area OMR & Sriperumbudur Axis
properties.baseline_text: 174 sq km built-up area
properties.comparison_text: 512 sq km built-up area
properties.delta_text: +338 sq km (+194.3%) expansion over coastal marshlands
properties.primary_driver: IT Corridor (OMR), automotive manufacturing hub along NH 48, suburban sprawl
properties.ecological_impact: Encroachment on the Pallikaranai freshwater marshland (shrank from 50 sq km to <5 sq km) and blocking of surplus flood canals connecting Chembarambakkam tank to Adyar River, directly causing the catastrophic 2015 Chennai floods.
properties.citation: Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA); Anna University Institute of Remote Sensing

properties.name: Sagar & Mousuni Island Coastal Front
properties.baseline_text: Intact coastal sand dune barriers and agricultural dykes
properties.comparison_text: 60.5% of coastline under active erosion (16–20 m/year)
properties.delta_text: Severe retreat >1.2 km; 60.5% of state coast eroding
properties.primary_driver: Sea level rise (~3.14 mm/yr), high macrotidal energy, and intense cyclone storm surges
properties.ecological_impact: Rapid shoreline retreat has washed away thousands of hectares of fertile farmland; neighboring Ghoramara Island has shrunk by over 50%, generating India's first documented climate-displaced refugees.
properties.citation: National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR / MoES) — Shoreline Change Atlas of India (1990-2018)

properties.name: Kendrapara & Satabhaya Coastal Ingress
properties.baseline_text: Satabhaya 7-village cluster located 1.5 km inland from high tide line
properties.comparison_text: Shoreline retreated >1.5 km; entire original village submerged
properties.delta_text: Sea ingress of >1.5 km; historic village completely inundated
properties.primary_driver: High wave energy, severe cyclonic erosion, and deficit in deltaic river sediment discharge
properties.ecological_impact: All 7 historical hamlets of Satabhaya were swallowed by the advancing sea, forcing the Odisha government to undertake India's first planned coastal community relocation to Bagapatia.
properties.citation: NCCR Ministry of Earth Sciences; Integrated Coastal Zone Management Project (ICZMP) Odisha

properties.name: Chellanam & Alappuzha Shoreline Retreat
properties.baseline_text: Continuous natural beach system with seasonal mudbank (Chakara) buffers
properties.comparison_text: 46.4% of Kerala coastline classified under active erosion
properties.delta_text: 46.4% state coast eroding; coastal roads frequently breached
properties.primary_driver: Monsoon swell wave attack, littoral drift obstruction by harbor breakwaters, sand mining
properties.ecological_impact: Frequent sea surges smash traditional granite seawalls and flood densely populated coastal fishing hamlets, destroying drinking water wells and necessitating expensive tetrapod seawalls.
properties.citation: NCCR Shoreline Change Assessment; Kerala State Coastal Area Development Corporation

properties.name: Puducherry & Ennore Port Downdrift Shoreline
properties.baseline_text: Broad 150m wide sandy beach along Promenade (Puducherry)
properties.comparison_text: Beach completely lost; 8 km coastline stripped to bedrock
properties.delta_text: 100% loss of natural beach width; artificial reef restoration active
properties.primary_driver: Harbor breakwater construction blocking northward littoral sand drift (0.6 million m³/yr)
properties.ecological_impact: Trapping of sand south of the harbor led to severe sediment starvation north of the port, stripping the famous Promenade beach down to black rocks until modern submerged artificial reefs were deployed for nourishment.
properties.citation: National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT); NCCR MoES

properties.name: Gulf of Khambhat Estuarine Bluff Collapse
properties.baseline_text: Stable estuarine mudflats and mangrove fringes
properties.comparison_text: 27.2% of Gujarat coastline under active erosion / dynamic scour
properties.delta_text: Macrotidal channel bank collapse & mudflat erosion
properties.primary_driver: Extreme macrotidal range (>10 meters) generating powerful scour currents in Narmada/Tapi mouths
properties.ecological_impact: Tidal bore currents undermine soft alluvial coastal bluffs, eroding hundreds of acres of coastal pasture and altering shallow navigational channels.
properties.citation: NCCR Shoreline Dynamics Atlas; Gujarat Institute of Desert Ecology (GUIDE)

properties.name: Chilika Lake Lagoon (Ramsar Site #229)
properties.baseline_text: 890 sq km open water; choke-up of outer channel; 350 sq km weed choked
properties.comparison_text: 1,165 sq km revived water spread; restored salinity gradient
properties.delta_text: +275 sq km (+30.9%) ecological recovery post-2000 dredging
properties.primary_driver: Hydrological engineering: cutting of new artificial sea mouth at Sipakuda in Sept 2000
properties.ecological_impact: A landmark global success in wetland restoration: opening the new tidal mouth flushed freshwater weeds, restored brackish salinity, and led to a six-fold increase in fish and prawn catch while safeguarding the endangered Irrawaddy Dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris).
properties.citation: Chilika Development Authority (CDA); Ramsar Convention Secretariat (Ramsar Wetland Conservation Award)

properties.name: Vembanad-Kol Wetland System (Ramsar Site #1214)
properties.baseline_text: 230 sq km open water expanse
properties.comparison_text: 148 sq km open water spread
properties.delta_text: -82 sq km (-35.65%) shrinkage via polders & weed matting
properties.primary_driver: Land reclamation for tourism/paddy, Thanneermukkom salinity barrage, African payal (water hyacinth) invasion
properties.ecological_impact: India's longest lake has lost over 35% of its water storage capacity. The Thanneermukkom bund permanently cut off natural estuarine tidal flushing, leading to severe eutrophication, toxic pesticide accumulation, and fish population crashes.
properties.citation: SAC - ISRO National Wetland Atlas: Kerala; Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment

properties.name: Wular Lake Natural Flood Basin (Ramsar Site #461)
properties.baseline_text: 89 sq km open water spread
properties.comparison_text: 38 sq km open water spread
properties.delta_text: -51 sq km (-57.3%) drastic contraction of open water
properties.primary_driver: Extensive willow (Salix) tree plantations, heavy siltation from catchments, agricultural encroachment
properties.ecological_impact: Contraction of this vital flood-absorption reservoir crippled its ability to buffer the Jhelum River during cloudbursts, contributing directly to the devastating catastrophic Kashmir floods of September 2014.
properties.citation: Wular Conservation and Management Authority (WUCMA); SAC - ISRO National Wetland Atlas

properties.name: Loktak Lake & Phumdis (Ramsar Site #468)
properties.baseline_text: Seasonal water-level oscillation supporting buoyant organic phumdis mats
properties.comparison_text: Permanent inundation; Montreux Record endangered wetland status
properties.delta_text: Permanent high water altering phumdis biomass & habitat
properties.primary_driver: Commissioning of the Ithai Barrage for hydroelectric power holding water levels high year-round
properties.ecological_impact: Permanent stagnation prevented the floating phumdis vegetation from grounding during winter to absorb nutrients. Thinning phumdis threatens the only natural habitat of the critically endangered Brow-antlered Deer (Sangai).
properties.citation: Loktak Development Authority (LDA); Ramsar Montreux Record Dossier

properties.name: Kolleru Lake Wetland (Ramsar Site #1209)
properties.baseline_text: 180 sq km lake area heavily encroached by illegal commercial fish ponds (>60% bed)
properties.comparison_text: 220 sq km partially restored open water following 'Operation Kolleru'
properties.delta_text: +40 sq km reclaimed water; ongoing agro-chemical runoff
properties.primary_driver: Massive commercial aquaculture tank proliferation followed by Supreme Court demolition drives
properties.ecological_impact: Demolition of fish tanks during 'Operation Kolleru' in 2006 restored partial open water for migratory pelicans and painted storks, but heavy agricultural pesticide and fertilizer runoff via Tammileru drain continues to degrade water quality.
properties.citation: Andhra Pradesh Forest Department Wildlife Wing; SAC - ISRO Wetland Inventory

properties.name: Sambhar Salt Lake (Ramsar Site #464)
properties.baseline_text: 230 sq km saline wetland catchment area
properties.comparison_text: 160 sq km open water spread
properties.delta_text: -70 sq km (-30.4%) open brine water shrinkage
properties.primary_driver: Proliferation of unauthorized commercial sub-surface borewell pumping of brine
properties.ecological_impact: India's largest inland salt lake suffers from depleted groundwater tables and altered salinity dynamics, creating anaerobic conditions that triggered avian botulism outbreaks killing thousands of migratory waterfowl in 2019.
properties.citation: Rajasthan State Wetland Authority; SAC - ISRO Wetland Atlas

properties.name: Thar Desert Eastern Transition Fringe
properties.baseline_text: 68.4% of district area under active land degradation
properties.comparison_text: 66.8% under active degradation (stabilization along canal belts)
properties.delta_text: -1.6% net stabilization via Indira Gandhi Canal shelterbelts
properties.primary_driver: Severe wind erosion, mobile sand dune shifts, and overgrazing by livestock
properties.ecological_impact: Active dune movement continually threatens roads and settlements; afforestation shelterbelts of Acacia and Prosopis cineraria along the Indira Gandhi Canal command area have helped stabilize mobile sands locally.
properties.citation: SAC - ISRO Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India (2003-05 to 2018-19); CAZRI Jodhpur

properties.name: Aravalli Range Mining Gap Corridors
properties.region: Rajasthan & Haryana (Alwar, Mahendragarh, Nuh, Gurugram border)
properties.baseline_text: Continuous natural rocky hill barrier containing western desert winds
properties.comparison_text: 12 distinct physical gaps created by illegal quartzite mining
properties.delta_text: 12 micro-gap breaches allowing desert sand drift into NCR
properties.primary_driver: Unchecked illegal stone quarrying, quartzite mining, and deforestation of ridge gaps
properties.ecological_impact: The ancient Aravalli Range is India's principal physical barrier shielding the northern plains from the Thar Desert. Breaches allow dry desert winds and sand dunes to migrate eastward towards southern Haryana and Delhi NCR.
properties.citation: Supreme Court of India Central Empowered Committee (CEC) Reports; Wildlife Institute of India (WII)

properties.name: Rayalaseema & Marathwada Rain-Shadow Belt
properties.baseline_text: 38.2% of geographic area degraded (sheet erosion)
properties.comparison_text: 44.5% of geographic area degraded
properties.delta_text: +6.3% increase in degraded scrub & drought-stressed lands
properties.primary_driver: Severe rain-shadow drought, soil moisture exhaustion, loss of traditional millets for groundnut monoculture
properties.ecological_impact: Anantapur has the second lowest rainfall in mainland India (after Jaisalmer). Recurrent drought cycles and heavy water-sheet erosion on barren red soils have turned vast tracts into semi-desert scrublands.
properties.citation: SAC - ISRO Desertification Atlas 2021; National Institute of Rural Development (NIRDPR)

properties.name: Chambal River Ravine & Gully Badlands
properties.region: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh (Morena, Bhind, Dholpur, Etawah)
properties.baseline_text: 4,800 sq km deeply entrenched badland ravines
properties.comparison_text: 5,120 sq km active headward ravine expansion
properties.delta_text: +320 sq km expansion; headward gully retreat of 0.5–1 m/yr
properties.primary_driver: Catastrophic water gully erosion in soft alluvial-lacustrine soils along deep river bluffs
properties.ecological_impact: Headward gully erosion continuously engulfs fertile agricultural tablelands, slicing productive topsoil into uncultivable 20-30 meter deep labyrinthine chasms.
properties.citation: Central Soil and Water Conservation Research and Training Institute (CSWCRTI); SAC - ISRO

properties.name: Little Rann & Banni Invasive Prosopis Transition
properties.baseline_text: Native saline grasslands supporting endemic Indian Wild Ass (Khur)
properties.comparison_text: Over 58% of grassland invaded by dense Prosopis juliflora thickets
properties.delta_text: +16% grassland displacement by invasive woody scrub
properties.primary_driver: Soil salinization, vegetative degradation, aggressive spread of invasive *Prosopis juliflora* (*Gando Baval*)
properties.ecological_impact: Invasive thorny scrub has choked the Asia's largest natural grassland (Banni), crowding out indigenous perennial grass species and compressing the critical grazing habitat of the endangered Indian Wild Ass.
properties.citation: Gujarat Institute of Desert Ecology (GUIDE); SAC - ISRO Desertification Atlas

properties.name: Indo-Gangetic Northwestern Granary Aquifers
properties.region: Punjab & Haryana (Sangrur, Moga, Barnala, Karnal, Kurukshetra)
properties.baseline_text: 145% Stage of Groundwater Extraction (Over-Exploited)
properties.comparison_text: 164% Stage of Groundwater Extraction in Punjab (76% blocks Over-Exploited)
properties.delta_text: +19% surge in extraction stress; water table falling 0.5–1 m/yr
properties.primary_driver: Unmetered free electricity for deep submersible tubewells, water-thirsty summer paddy monoculture
properties.ecological_impact: Pumping groundwater at nearly double the natural annual monsoon recharge rate has dried up shallow unconfined aquifers, forcing farmers to bore down 150-200 meters into saline deeper strata and triggering urgent state preservation acts.
properties.citation: Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) — Dynamic Ground Water Resources of India 2004 & 2022

properties.name: Marwar Arid Deep Fossil Aquifers
properties.baseline_text: 138% Stage of Extraction
properties.comparison_text: 188% Stage of Extraction (Critical Over-Draft)
properties.delta_text: +50% extraction leap; extensive mining of non-renewable fossil water
properties.primary_driver: Low rainfall (<300 mm/yr), non-replenishable deep sandstone aquifers, cash crop tubewell cultivation
properties.ecological_impact: Aquifers are being irreversibly depleted. Pumping deep ancient groundwater mobilizes dangerously high fluoride and total dissolved solids (TDS), creating widespread fluorosis bone deformities among rural communities.
properties.citation: CGWB National Compilation 2022; Ground Water Department, Govt of Rajasthan

properties.name: Delhi Metropolitan & Yamuna Floodplain Aquifers
properties.region: Delhi NCT (South, Southwest, New Delhi, West Districts)
properties.baseline_text: 110% Stage of Groundwater Extraction
properties.comparison_text: 119% Stage of Extraction; 15 of 34 tehsils Over-Exploited
properties.delta_text: +9% increase; deep localized drawdown depression cones
properties.primary_driver: Urban population growth, illegal borewells in unpiped colonies, concrete paving blocking rain infiltration
properties.ecological_impact: Water table depth in parts of South Delhi and Gurugram exceeds 40-60 meters below ground level; heavy extraction along Yamuna floodplains risks saline groundwater ingress from surrounding semi-arid formations.
properties.citation: CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resources 2022; Delhi Jal Board (DJB)

properties.name: Western Tamil Nadu Hard-Rock Aquifers (Noyyal/Cauvery)
properties.baseline_text: 115% Stage of Groundwater Extraction
properties.comparison_text: 135% Stage of Extraction in hard crystalline rocks
properties.delta_text: +20% extraction surge in low-porosity gneiss rocks
properties.primary_driver: Intensive industrial textile bleaching/dyeing abstraction and commercial horticultural irrigation
properties.ecological_impact: Crystalline gneissic bedrock provides very poor aquifer storage; borewells drilled to depths >300 meters frequently yield dry holes while industrial effluents have contaminated shallow recharge zones.
properties.citation: CGWB State Report: Tamil Nadu 2022; Tamil Nadu Water Supply and Drainage Board (TWAD)

properties.name: Eastern Gangetic Alluvial Aquifers & Arsenic Threat
properties.region: Bihar & West Bengal (Patna, Purnea, Malda, Murshidabad)
properties.baseline_text: 38% Stage of Extraction (Classified as Safe volumetric balance)
properties.comparison_text: 46% Stage of Extraction (Abundant volumetric recharge)
properties.delta_text: +8% extraction; high geogenic Arsenic water quality crisis
properties.primary_driver: Shallow tubewell pumping mobilizing naturally occurring geogenic arsenic from Holocene sediments
properties.ecological_impact: While quantitative volumetric recharge is abundant and 'Safe' (<50%), millions of rural villagers drink from shallow tubewells contaminated with arsenic exceeding the 10 µg/L WHO limit, leading to widespread hyperkeratosis and skin cancers.
properties.citation: CGWB Ground Water Quality in India; School of Environmental Studies, Jadavpur University

properties.name: Kosi River 120 km Westward Avulsion Corridor
properties.baseline_text: Historical course flowed through Purnea (James Rennell 1760 Survey)
properties.comparison_text: Contemporary active braided belt near Supaul (120 km west)
properties.delta_text: 120 km westward migration in 250 years + 2008 Kusaha breach
properties.primary_driver: Enormous silt load (100 million m³/yr) originating in eastern Himalayas causing rapid aggradation and avulsion
properties.ecological_impact: The classic 'Sorrow of Bihar'. On 18 August 2008, the river breached the eastern embankment at Kusaha (Nepal) and avulsed 100 km eastward into an ancient abandoned channel, inundating 400,000 hectares and displacing 3.3 million people.
properties.citation: National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC / ISRO); Central Water Commission (CWC) Fluvial Geomorphology Studies

properties.name: Brahmaputra Channel Widening & Majuli Island Shrinkage
properties.baseline_text: Majuli Island area ~750 sq km (post-1950 Assam M8.6 earthquake)
properties.comparison_text: Majuli Island contracted to ~380 sq km; braided width 15-18 km
properties.delta_text: -49.3% reduction in island landmass via bankline toe erosion
properties.primary_driver: Massive earthquake co-seismic landslides raising riverbed, high monsoon peak discharges (>70,000 m³/s)
properties.ecological_impact: World's largest river island and cradle of Vaishnavite Neo-Vaishnavism culture has lost over half its geographical area. Continuous bankline erosion forces historic Satras (monasteries) to repeatedly relocate inland.
properties.citation: Brahmaputra Board, Ministry of Jal Shakti; NRSC Assam Water Resources Satellite Mapping

properties.name: Ganga Bankline Migration at Malda & Murshidabad
properties.baseline_text: Symmetrical meandering channel prior to Farakka Barrage impoundment
properties.comparison_text: Severe left-bank migration; Manikchak & Bhutanir Char erosion
properties.delta_text: 3.5 km bankline displacement; dynamic char island generation
properties.primary_driver: Backwater siltation upstream of Farakka barrage, soft uncohesive silty riverbank scouring
properties.ecological_impact: Severe bank erosion swallows whole mouzas and agricultural lands in Malda's Manikchak and Kaliachak blocks, creating shifting temporary river islands (chars) whose inhabitants face stateless ambiguity across the WB-Jharkhand border.
properties.citation: Farakka Barrage Project (CWC); Centre for Earth Science Studies (CESS)

properties.name: Vedic Saraswati / Ghaggar-Hakra Paleochannel Network
properties.region: Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat (Adi Badri to Rann of Kutch)
properties.baseline_text: Perennial snow-fed glacial river connecting Shivaliks to Arabian Sea (c. 3000 BCE)
properties.comparison_text: Subterranean buried sand paleochannel identified by ISRO satellite sensors
properties.delta_text: Total surface river desiccation via tectonic Yamuna/Sutlej diversion
properties.primary_driver: Tectonic uplift of the Aravalli-Delhi ridge capturing glacial headwaters into the Yamuna and Sutlej
properties.ecological_impact: Loss of the glacial headwaters transformed the fertile Saraswati-Drishadvati basin into the hyper-arid Thar Desert, prompting the dispersal of Mature Harappan urban centers eastward into the Gangetic plain.
properties.citation: ISRO SAC Paleochannel Atlas (IRS WiFS / LISS-III); Geological Society of India Memoir 42

properties.name: Teesta River Historic 1787 Megaflood Avulsion
properties.region: West Bengal & Bangladesh (Jalpaiguri, Rangpur, Jamuna confluence)
properties.baseline_text: Teesta flowed south via Karatoya into the Ganga (Padma)
properties.comparison_text: Avulsed 90 km eastward to join the Brahmaputra (Jamuna)
properties.delta_text: Catastrophic 90 km nodal shift during the July 1787 megaflood
properties.primary_driver: Immense tectonic-sediment choking during catastrophic monsoonal floods of 1787
properties.ecological_impact: A single megaflood event completely altered the hydrological geography of Bengal: the Teesta deserted its southern course to the Ganga, joining the Brahmaputra and forcing the Brahmaputra itself to avulse into the new Jamuna channel.
properties.citation: CWC Historical River Avulsion Records; James Rennell Bengal Atlas (1779); GSI Eastern Region
